cards.q: Which comment syntax spans several lines?
cards.a: `--[[` up to `]]`. Two dashes alone comment to the end of one line.
cards.lessonTitle: What Lua Is and Running Code

cards.q: A program has a syntax error on line 30. Does lines 1 to 29 run first?
cards.a: No. Lua reads the whole file first; a syntax error means nothing runs. A run-time error stops the program partway, after the lines before it have run.
cards.lessonTitle: What Lua Is and Running Code

cards.q: What does `type(type(5))` give?
cards.a: `"string"`: `type(5)` is the string `"number"`, and the type of a string is `"string"`.

cards.q: Why write local?
cards.a: Without it the variable is global: shared with the whole program and every library, slower, and easy to clash with.

cards.q: What are `10 / 2` and `10 // 2`?
cards.a: `5.0` and `5`. `/` always gives a float; `//` with two integers gives an integer.

cards.q: How do you test whether n is even?
cards.a: `n % 2 == 0`. It works for negative numbers too, because `%` takes the sign of the divisor.

cards.q: What is `#"hello" .. "!"`?
cards.a: `"5!"`: `#` binds tighter than `..`, so it is `5 .. "!"`.

cards.q: Which writes no newline: print or io.write?
cards.a: io.write. It writes exactly its arguments.

cards.q: What is Lua's "not equal" operator?
Does `if 0 then` run its body?
cards.a: Yes. Only false and nil are false; 0 is true.

cards.q: How many times does `for i = 1, 10, 2` run?
cards.a: Five: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The next value, 11, is past 10.

cards.q: What is the difference between while and repeat?
cards.a: while tests before each round and may run zero times; repeat tests after, so it runs at least once, and it stops when the condition becomes true.

cards.q: How do you read the last item of a list t?
Why is `t[2] = nil` a bad way to remove the second item?
cards.a: It leaves a hole: # and ipairs no longer see the items after it reliably. Use table.remove(t, 2).

cards.q: How do you remove a key from a table?
cards.a: Assign nil to it: `t.key = nil`.

cards.q: What is the difference between t.name and t[name]?
cards.a: `t.name` is the key "name"; `t[name]` uses the value of the variable name as the key.

cards.q: What does table.sort return?
cards.a: Nothing. It sorts the table you gave it, in place.

cards.q: How do you sort a list of numbers from largest to smallest?
cards.a: `table.sort(t, function(a, b) return a > b end)`.

cards.q: After `local b = a`, where a is a table, does changing b[1] change a?
cards.a: Yes. b and a are the same table; nothing was copied.

cards.q: What does a shallow copy not copy?
cards.a: The tables nested inside: the copy and the original still share them.

cards.q: What happens when you call a two-parameter function with one argument?
cards.a: The second parameter is nil. Lua never complains about the number of arguments.

cards.q: How do you keep only the first result of a call that returns several?
cards.a: Put the call in brackets, `(f())`, or use it anywhere other than last in a list.

cards.q: Why is `flag = flag or true` a bug?
cards.a: If the caller passes false, `false or true` is true, so false can never get through. Test `if flag == nil then flag = true end` instead.

cards.q: How many arguments did a function receive, counting nils?
What is a closure?
cards.a: A function together with the local variables from around it that it uses; they stay alive as long as the function does.

cards.q: Two counters from make_counter: do they share a count?
cards.a: No. Each call of make_counter creates a new count variable.

cards.q: Why does a recursive local function need `local function name`?
cards.a: So that the local name exists before the body is compiled, and the call inside the body refers to it rather than to a global.

cards.q: Is `return 1 + f(n - 1)` a tail call?
cards.a: No. The addition happens after f returns, so the current call must be kept.

cards.q: Where do global variables live?
cards.a: In the table _G: `x = 5` is the same as `_G.x = 5`.

cards.q: What does `<const>` do?
cards.a: Makes it a compile-time error to assign to that local after its declaration.

cards.q: What does ("hello"):sub(-3) give?
cards.a: "llo": the last three characters.

cards.q: Why pass true as the fourth argument of find?
cards.a: To search for plain text. Without it the search text is a pattern, and characters like . or - have special meanings.

cards.q: How do you match a literal dot?
cards.a: `%.`. A bare `.` matches any character.

cards.q: What is the difference between `.*` and `.-`?
cards.a: `.*` takes as much as possible, `.-` as little as possible.

cards.q: What two values does gsub return?
cards.a: The new string and the number of replacements.

cards.q: In a gsub replacement string, what is %1?
cards.a: The first capture of the match.

cards.q: How do you show 3.14159 as 3.14?
cards.a: `string.format("%.2f", 3.14159)`.

cards.q: Which flag aligns a value to the left of its width?
Why is #"é" 2?
cards.a: # counts bytes, and é takes two bytes in UTF-8.

cards.q: How do you count the characters of a UTF-8 string?
cards.a: `utf8.len(s)`.

cards.q: What does setmetatable return?
cards.a: The table you gave it, now with its metatable set.

cards.q: Which metamethod does print use?
cards.a: `__tostring` (print calls tostring).

cards.q: When is __newindex called?
cards.a: When assigning to a key the table does not have yet. Assigning to an existing key does not call it.

cards.q: What are rawget and rawset for?
cards.a: Reading and writing a table without its metamethods, for example from inside __index or __newindex.

cards.q: What does `function Account:deposit(n)` mean?
cards.a: `function Account.deposit(self, n)`: the colon adds a first parameter called self.

cards.q: Why does `Account.__index = Account` make methods work?
cards.a: Objects do not have method fields. A missing key on an object is looked up through its metatable's __index, which is the class, where the methods are.

cards.q: How does a Dog method call Animal's version of the same method?
cards.a: `Animal.method(self, ...)`: call it through the base class with a dot and pass self.

cards.q: What makes Dog fall back to Animal?
cards.a: `setmetatable(Dog, { __index = Animal })`.

cards.q: What should the last line of a module file be?
cards.a: `return M`: the table holding the module's public functions.

cards.q: What happens the second time a program requires the same module?
cards.a: Nothing is loaded again: require returns the same table, stored in package.loaded.

cards.q: What does error(msg, 2) change?
cards.a: The position added to the message: level 2 points at the caller of the function, not the error line itself.

cards.q: What does pcall return when the function fails?
cards.a: `false` and the error value.

cards.q: When does a generic for loop stop?
cards.a: When the iterator returns nil as its first value.

cards.q: How do you check whether a table is empty?
cards.a: `next(t) == nil`. # only measures the list part.

cards.q: What does coroutine.yield(x) do?
cards.a: Pauses the coroutine and makes the resume that ran it return true and x.

cards.q: What is the difference between create and wrap?
cards.a: create returns a coroutine you run with resume (which returns a success flag); wrap returns a function that resumes it and returns the yielded values directly.

cards.q: What does io.open("x.txt", "w") do to an existing x.txt?
cards.a: Empties it. Use "a" to add to the end instead.

cards.q: What does `local f <close> = ...` guarantee?
cards.a: f is closed when the block ends, whether it ends normally or with an error.

cards.q: How does a C function return two values to Lua?
cards.a: It pushes both onto the stack and returns 2.

cards.q: What does a host leave out to stop scripts from touching files?
cards.a: The io and os libraries (it opens only the libraries it wants, instead of luaL_openlibs).

cards.q: What does a free name like `width` mean inside a chunk?
cards.a: `_ENV.width`: a field of the chunk's environment, which is `_G` unless something else was given.

cards.q: Why pass `"t"` as the mode to `load`?
cards.a: It refuses precompiled bytecode, which can be crafted to crash or attack the Lua interpreter.

cards.q: Why does an ordinary table used as a cache leak memory?
cards.a: It references every object stored in it, so none of them can ever become unreachable and be collected.
cards.lessonTitle: Weak Tables and the Garbage Collector

cards.q: When should a resource be released with `__close` rather than `__gc`?
cards.a: When it must be released at a known moment: `__close` runs when the variable goes out of scope, `__gc` whenever the collector gets to it.
cards.lessonTitle: Weak Tables and the Garbage Collector

cards.q: What is `-7 // 2` in Lua?
cards.a: `-4`: floor division rounds down, towards negative infinity.
cards.lessonTitle: Integers, Bitwise Operators and Binary Data

cards.q: What is the difference between `a ~ b` and `~a`?
cards.a: `a ~ b` is exclusive OR of two values; `~a` flips every bit of one value.
cards.lessonTitle: Integers, Bitwise Operators and Binary Data
